claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified now because aggregate readiness passed and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, provided the unresolved procurement invoice review limitation is explicitly disclosed and monitored post-deployment.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the limitation is explicitly disclosed in final launch materials, the actor's position becomes materially stronger.
If admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance with the required fields, the certification basis becomes materially stronger.
If admissible evidence shows the slice issue is resolved or no longer material, the main policy concern is removed.
Absent disclosure, approved mitigation, or approved risk acceptance, certification remains inadequately supported under the stated policy threshold.
evidence_requests: Final model card or launch packet showing the procurement invoice review limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Approved mitigation or risk-acceptance record with accountable owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Materiality determination for whether the procurement invoice review slice issue qualifies as a material limitation for the named launch use case.
Approval record showing certification is authorized despite the unresolved slice issue, if such approval exists.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows a current unresolved slice weakness in a named launch use case, concentrated in exception-code classification.
The mitigation artifact is only a draft runbook and lacks a defined owner and alert threshold, so it does not satisfy the policy condition for an approved mitigation.
The current model-card draft states there are no known material limitations, which conflicts with the actor's certification rationale unless the disclosure is actually updated before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that an approved risk acceptance exists or that the required limitation disclosure has been incorporated into the final launch materials.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support general readiness, but they do not by themselves resolve the disclosure predicate in policy_text.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable on the existing record, because the record does not show the required limitation disclosure has actually been made.
That post-deployment monitoring meaningfully closes the policy gap, because the cited monitoring artifact is still draft and unapproved.
Any implication that the current packet already satisfies model-card disclosure requirements for this launch use case.
